name: Lokalise Nightly QA Report to #i18n-team
description: Every night at 02:00 (Europe/Madrid): counts Lokalise QA issues per project for inconsistent placeholders and inconsistent HTML, and posts a per-project count report to the private #i18n-team Slack channel.

parameters.content:
## Nightly Lokalise QA check
Runs at 02:00 Europe/Madrid. **Summary** message to #i18n-team plus **threaded** per-project detail with clickable Lokalise links and **the locales behind each count**. Alphabetical; clean projects suppressed but counted.

**Three checks:** Placeholders, HTML, Double space. Brackets, numbers and email checks are intentionally excluded.

**Locales are derived here, not by Lokalise.** `filter_qa_issues` returns flagged KEYS with no per-language attribution, and `filter_translation_lang_ids` is silently ignored on it. So the workflow requests `include_translations=1` on all three checks and works out the locale itself: for **Placeholders** and **HTML** it compares each target's placeholder / tag inventory against the source and names the targets that differ; for **Double space** the attribution is exact. The COUNT is Lokalise's (flagged keys, archived removed) and stays authoritative; the locale split is ours. Where the two disagree the difference shows as `N unattributed` - that is a key Lokalise flagged whose locale our comparison could not pin down (usually an empty target or a placeholder style the regex does not model). Empty targets and pseudo `pst` are never blamed.

**Double space is target-only.** EN source is not reported at all, and a key is ignored entirely if the source also has the double space - that's inherited from the repo, not translator-introduced. The check is also **not run on html/legal-pages projects** (name contains `html` or `legal page`), where double spaces are indentation in HTML rather than defects. Placeholders and HTML still run everywhere.

**Archived keys are excluded client-side.** `filter_qa_issues` silently IGNORES `filter_archived` (exclude/include/only all return the same count), so the `x-pagination-total-count` header includes archived keys and does NOT match the Lokalise UI. The workflow fetches keys with limit=500 and counts `is_archived == false`. Do not revert to reading the header.

A control request with a deliberately invalid filter value runs once per execution; Lokalise returns 400 for it, proving the QA filter is actually applied and the zeros are real. Throttled to ~4.5 req/s under the Lokalise 10 req/s limit.

## Second message: typos + brand names in targets

> :no_entry: **CURRENTLY DISABLED — does not run in the nightly.**
> `Run Typo + Brand Scan` and `Post Typo Report` are both switched off. The sub-workflow `NZx0HhFB3QkcBYPh` is unpublished, and n8n refuses to publish a parent whose sub-workflow is still a draft. To turn this on: publish the sub-workflow, re-enable `Run Typo + Brand Scan`, then publish this workflow.
>
> :warning: **Leave `Post Typo Report` disabled.** The sub-workflow posts its own Slack message and returns the Slack API response (`ok`, `channel`, `ts`) — it never returns `typo_message`. That node could only ever fail with `no_text`, and it failed the whole execution. Only re-enable it if the sub-workflow is changed to return text instead of posting.

When enabled: after the placeholder/HTML/double-space report and its thread, the nightly calls **Lokalise - target typo scan (sub)**, which posts its own **separate** message to #i18n-team showing project name and count per language.

**Scope:** TARGET languages only (source and pseudo `pst` excluded). **HTML projects are excluded by name** (`/html/i`) - 5 of them today. Gated on Lokalise's own `spelling_and_grammar` filter, so it is a subset of what that UI filter shows; real typos its dictionary misses will not appear here.

**"High ranked" is computed here, not by Lokalise.** `filter_qa_issues` returns flagged KEYS with no per-language attribution and no severity - `filter_translation_lang_ids` is silently ignored on it. So both the per-language split and the ranking are derived client-side in the page sub-workflow.

**Five rules, tuned for precision over recall:** `repeated_word` (per-language stoplists, since French `vous vous` and German `die die` are correct), `triple_letter` (consonant triples skipped for compounding languages, vowel triples for Tagalog/Romanian), `mixed_script` (Latin/Cyrillic/Greek homoglyphs - zero false positives so far), `brand_misspelled` and `brand_case` (from the 17 non-translatable glossary terms). Untuned, the same rules produced 2995 findings, ~95% of them legitimate grammar; tuned, 112.

**Known trade-off:** brand errors confined to the last 2 characters are NOT reported, because a case ending (Czech `App Storu`, Finnish `QRcreaten`) cannot be told from a final-letter typo without morphology.

**Memory:** fetching 22k flagged keys with translations in one execution OOMs. Each 500-key page is fetched and reduced to findings in its own sub-execution. Do not inline it back.
